items.q: Delirium tremens typically begins how long after last drink?
items.exp: DT emerges two to four days into withdrawal with delirium, fever and autonomic instability, distinct from early tremor and day one seizures. Untreated mortality historically high; benzodiazepines and supportive care treat it.
r: Incorrect. Two hours is intoxication or early tremor.
Correct. Forty eight to ninety six hours.
Incorrect. Two weeks is beyond withdrawal syndrome.
Incorrect. Immediate is intoxication phase.
items.kp: Day three confused and stormy equals DT.

items.q: Before giving IV glucose to a malnourished dependent drinker, what must be given and why?
o: Parenteral thiamine; prevent precipitating Wernicke encephalopathy
items.exp: Glucose load consumes thiamine in metabolism and can precipitate or worsen Wernicke in deficient patients, so parenteral B vitamins precede or accompany glucose in at risk patients per local protocol.
r: Incorrect. Insulin follows glucose monitoring, not this rule.
Correct. Thiamine before glucose.
Incorrect. Sepsis treatment does not precede metabolically.
Incorrect. Sedation treats withdrawal but not this metabolic trap.

items.q: Confusion, ataxia and nystagmus in a homeless drinker diagnose which emergency, and full triad frequency?
o: Wernicke encephalopathy; full triad present in minority
items.exp: Wernicke presents variably: only minority show complete classic triad, so suspicion alone mandates immediate parenteral thiamine. Korsakoff is chronic amnesic aftermath, not acute eye sign stage.
r: Incorrect. Korsakoff is chronic amnesia, triad is Wernicke.
Correct. Wernicke, treat without full triad.
Incorrect. Fever and autonomic storm define DT differently.
Incorrect. Hepatic flap differs and eye signs absent.
items.kp: Treat Wernicke on a hint, not full house.

items.q: Korsakoff syndrome core deficit is what?
o: Anterograde amnesia with confabulation, other cognition relatively spared
items.exp: Diencephalic injury blocks new memory formation while remote memory and intellect relatively persist, filled gaps by plausible confabulation without intent to deceive. Rehabilitation uses memory aids and structured environments.
r: Incorrect. Deficit is strikingly memory selective.
Correct. New learning lost, confabulation fills.
Incorrect. Language otherwise intact.
Incorrect. No focal motor lesion.
items.kp: Cannot lay new memories, invents to fill.

items.q: Auditory hallucinations in clear consciousness 36 hours after stopping alcohol, without confusion, indicate what?
items.exp: Hallucinosis in withdrawal window with clear sensorium (often derogatory voices) contrasts DT delirium with visual hallucinations and autonomic storm. It usually resolves days, occasionally persists.
r: Incorrect. DT clouds consciousness with fever.
Correct. Clear consciousness hallucinosis.
Incorrect. Timing and clarity point withdrawal state.
Incorrect. Wernicke confuses with eye and gait signs.
items.kp: Clear mind hearing voices day two: hallucinosis.

items.q: Drug best matched to maintaining abstinence via anti craving glutamate modulation, dosed with meals, renal caution, is what?
items.exp: Acamprosate supports abstinence after detoxification, started after withdrawal, renally cleared. Naltrexone reduces heavy drinking days; disulfiram is aversive; methadone treats opioid dependence.
r: Incorrect. Disulfiram punishes drinking via acetaldehyde.
Correct. Acamprosate for abstinence support.
Incorrect. Naltrexone opioid antagonist reduces reward.
Incorrect. Methadone is opioid substitution.

items.q: Patient on naltrexone for alcohol needs emergency opioid analgesia after trauma. Key issue is what?
o: Opioid blockade reduces analgesia; specialist pain plan needed, and naltrexone must stop before elective opioids
items.exp: Mu blockade blunts opioid analgesia and precipitates withdrawal in opioid dependent patients; elective surgery planning stops naltrexone in advance (oral days, injection weeks per guidance) and trauma needs anaesthetic led alternatives or high dose monitored opioids.
r: Incorrect. Interaction is major.
Correct. Blockade complicates opioid analgesia.
Incorrect. Opposite effect occurs.
Incorrect. DT follows alcohol cessation, not naltrexone.

items.q: CAGE screening questions stand for Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty and what?
items.exp: Eye opener (needing morning drink to steady nerves or cure hangover) signals dependence physiology. Two or more yes answers raise concern, though AUDIT quantifies better.
r: Incorrect. Not part of mnemonic.
Correct. Eye opener morning drink.
Incorrect. Appetite not in CAGE.
Incorrect. Exercise unrelated.

items.q: Supervised disulfiram is appropriate only when patient is what?
o: Motivated, abstinent, fully informed and medically screened, with supervision
items.exp: Disulfiram requires abstinence goal, consent understanding reaction (flushing, vomiting, hypotension with alcohol including sauces and aftershave), cardiac and liver screening and supervised adherence; covert administration is unethical and dangerous.
r: Incorrect. Drinking on it is dangerous without intent.
Correct. Motivated abstinent informed supervised.
Incorrect. Avoid in pregnancy.
Incorrect. Covert dosing is prohibited.
items.kp: Disulfiram only with knowing willing quitter.

items.q: Withdrawal seizure prophylaxis and treatment in dependent drinkers rely mainly on which drug class?
items.exp: Benzodiazepines substitute GABAergic alcohol effect with taper preventing seizures and DT, dosed by fixed reducing or symptom triggered CIWA regimens. Antipsychotics lower seizure threshold and are adjuncts only for hallucinations with cover.
r: Incorrect. They may provoke seizures alone.
Correct. Benzodiazepine taper is backbone.
Incorrect. No withdrawal seizure protection.
Incorrect. Opioids irrelevant and harmful.
items.kp: Replace alcohol GABA smoothly with benzodiazepine taper.
